# piagent-realtime-provider-maxtokens

Rewrites the output limit of OpenRouter requests to the smallest limit among the
model's provider endpoints, so OpenRouter stops filtering out endpoints that
publish a lower limit than the catalogue maximum. Routing itself stays with
OpenRouter: no provider is pinned and `models.json` is never touched.

## Table of contents

- [Behavior](#behavior)
- [Installation](#installation)

## Behavior

OpenRouter only routes a request to providers that can serve a response of the
requested length. Pi sends `max_completion_tokens` (or `max_tokens`, depending on
the model's `compat.maxTokensField`) from `model.maxTokens`, and for OpenRouter
models that value is the model-wide maximum from the catalogue. Every endpoint
with a lower output limit is therefore removed before routing.

The extension rewrites that field in the outgoing payload to the smallest output
limit among the model's provider endpoints. The limit is read from OpenRouter's
public model endpoints route and cached per model on disk, so a request never
waits for a lookup.

Example, `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (31 endpoints, catalogue maximum 943718):

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `max_completion_tokens` sent | 943718 | 131072 |
| endpoints OpenRouter may route to | only those publishing the maximum | all 31 |

Nothing else changes: the request keeps its `provider` routing object, other
providers are untouched, and a failed or missing lookup falls back to the
configured cap instead of blocking the request.

The status bar shows `MT:<limit>` for the selected OpenRouter model, `MT:<limit>*`
while the fallback cap is in use, and `MT:off` when the extension is disabled.

## Installation

Local (development):

```bash
pi -e ./extensions/realtime-provider-maxtokens.ts
```

As a pi package (GitHub or npm):

```bash
pi install git:git@github.com:FloezWerk/piagent-realtime-provider-maxtokens.git
# or
pi install npm:@floez-werk/piagent-realtime-provider-maxtokens
```

The npm package is listed in the [pi package catalog](https://pi.dev/packages)
automatically (keyword `pi-package`).

## Commands

| Command | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `/provider-maxtokens` or `/provider-maxtokens status` | State, TTL, fallback cap, cache size, the selected model's cached limit, the value that will be sent, the last clamp and the clamp count of this session |
| `/provider-maxtokens on` | Rewrite outgoing payloads (persisted) |
| `/provider-maxtokens off` | Leave payloads untouched (persisted) |
| `/provider-maxtokens toggle` | Toggle (persisted) |
| `/provider-maxtokens refresh` | Re-resolve the limits of the session's scoped OpenRouter models |
| `/provider-maxtokens clear` | Drop the cache; requests use the fallback cap until the next lookup |
| `/provider-maxtokens ttl <minutes>` | Cache TTL in minutes (persisted, default 60) |
| `/provider-maxtokens cap <tokens>` | Fallback cap (persisted, default 131072) |

After changes in a running session: `/reload`.

## Configuration

Settings live under the root key `provider-maxtokens` in Pi's shared
`~/.pi/agent/settings.json` and are written by the commands above:

| Key | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | Rewrite the outgoing output limit |
| `ttlMinutes` | `60` | Age after which a cached limit is refreshed |
| `fallbackCap` | `131072` | Limit used when no fresh entry exists or a lookup fails |

The per-model cache is stored in `~/.pi/agent/provider-maxtokens-cache.json`.
Only the extension's own keys are written; the rest of the file is preserved.

## Dependencies

`@earendil-works/pi-ai`, `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` and
`@earendil-works/pi-tui` are bundled by pi and are therefore only declared as
`peerDependencies`.

<!-- changelog:start -->
<!-- Generated by pi-release sync-readme-changelog; edit CHANGELOG.md, not this block. -->
**0.1.0 - 2026-10-06**

### Added

- Rewrites the output limit (`max_completion_tokens`, or `max_tokens` when the
  model uses that field) in outgoing OpenRouter payloads to the smallest output
  limit among the model's provider endpoints. OpenRouter only routes to endpoints
  that can serve the requested length, and Pi sends the model-wide catalogue
  maximum - so endpoints publishing a lower limit were filtered out before
  routing.
- Resolves that limit from OpenRouter's public model endpoints route and caches it
  per model in `provider-maxtokens-cache.json`, so the request path never waits
  for a lookup.
- Refreshes a cached limit once it is older than the TTL (default: 60 minutes).
- Warms the cache for the session's scoped OpenRouter models on session start and
  for the selected model on a model switch.
- Falls back to a configurable cap when no fresh entry exists or a lookup fails,
  so requests keep working offline and for unknown models.
- Adds the `/provider-maxtokens` command with `status`, `on`, `off`, `toggle`,
  `refresh`, `clear`, `ttl <minutes>` and `cap <tokens>`.
- Adds the status bar entry `MT:<limit>` (`*` marks the fallback cap, `MT:off`
  when disabled).
- Adds settings under the root key `provider-maxtokens` in `settings.json`
  (`enabled`, `ttlMinutes`, `fallbackCap`).
- Leaves everything else alone: no provider is registered, `models.json` is
  neither read nor written, and no provider is pinned.

Full history and all versions: [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md)
<!-- changelog:end -->
